files.lesson.md: --- order: 12 unit: transform node: AC9M7SP03 n1 title: Translations summary: "A translation slides every point of a shape the same distance in the same direction. Right adds to x, left takes away; up adds to y, down takes away. The shape does not change size or turn." language: maths voice: { name: af_heart, speed: 1.1 } hook: "A chess piece slides across the board, a lift goes up, a character steps left on a screen. Each is a translation: every point moves the same way." connection: sprite-move app: command: node "$REPO_ROOT/tools/serve.mjs" "$REPO_ROOT/dist/_playground-board" 8297 url: http://127.0.0.1:8297/index.html readySelector: "#gsum" layout: full explainPicture: { ref: move.yml#explain-pic, caption: "The triangle moves 3 right and 2 down: every corner changes by $(+3, -2)$." } explainClip: query: { code: "@move.yml#explain", fresh: 1, id: explain } caption: "Slide, and read the change" say: "Every corner moves the same way." clip: - caption: { text: "A triangle, A at (1, 1).", say: "A triangle, with A at one, one." } - wait: 800 - caption: { text: "Move it 3 right.", say: "Move it three right." } - click: Make the move right bigger - click: Make the move right bigger - click: Make the move right bigger - caption: { text: "Now 2 down: every corner changes by the same amount.", say: "Now two down. Every corner changes by the same amount." } - click: Make the move up smaller - click: Make the move up smaller - expect: { selector: "#gsum", contains: "Translate 3 right, 2 down" } - wait: 1500 --- A **translation** slides a shape without turning or flipping it. Every point moves the same distance in the same direction, so the shape keeps its size and shape. The shape is called the **object** and its new position the **image**; a point A becomes A′ (said "A prime"). On the coordinate plane, a move right or up **adds** to a coordinate and a move left or down **takes away**. A translation of 3 right and 2 down changes $(x, y)$ to $(x + 3, y - 2)$. ## Predict: where does A land? ```step stage: predict insight: "Committing to the image of one point under 3 right and 2 down shows whether they add to the right coordinate in the right direction." check: type: predict q: "Point A is at (1, 1). The triangle is translated 3 right and 2 down. Where does A land?" options: ["(4, −1)", "(4, 3)", "(−2, −1)", "(3, 2)"] actual: "(4, −1). Right adds 3 to x: 1 + 3 = 4. Down takes 2 from y: 1 − 2 = −1." ``` Add to x for right, take from y for down. ## Run: slide the triangle ```step stage: run insight: "Sliding the triangle and reading each corner's change shows that the same amount is added to every x and to every y." try: { playground: board, starter: "move.yml#run", height: 600 } check: { type: board, text: "Slide the triangle until A′ is at (4, −1). Was your prediction right?", when: "x(A) = 4 and y(A) = -1", explain: "A moves 3 right and 2 down, so A′ is (1 + 3, 1 − 2) = (4, −1)." } ``` The orange triangle is the image. The panel lists every corner and where it goes. ## Investigate: reading the move ```step stage: investigate insight: "Right and up add, left and down take away (Ravi adds for left); every corner moves the same; the shape stays the same size." tasks: - check: type: question q: "The triangle has corners A (1, 1), B (3, 1) and C (3, 2). It moves 3 right and 2 down. Where does B land?" options: ["(6, −1)", "(6, 3)", "(0, −1)", "(4, −1)"] answer: 0 feedback: [null, "Down takes 2 away from y.", "Right adds 3 to x.", "That is where A lands."] explain: "B′ = (3 + 3, 1 − 2) = (6, −1)." - check: type: bug code: "working.txt#ravi" text: "Ravi translates A (2, 3) by 4 left and 1 up. Click the line where his reasoning goes wrong." answer: 2 fault: logic misconception: translate-sign explain: "Line 2: moving left makes x smaller, so take 4 away: 2 − 4 = −2. The image is (−2, 4)." - check: type: question q: "What stays the same when a shape is translated?" options: ["Its size, its shape and the way it faces", "Only its size", "Its position", "Its coordinates"] answer: 0 feedback: [null, "The shape and direction stay the same too.", "The position is what changes.", "Every coordinate changes."] explain: "A translation only changes the position. The image is congruent to the object." ``` ### Where does B land? Apply the same move to B. ### Find the mistake Read Ravi's working. Which way does x go when you move left? ### What stays the same ## Modify: choose the move ```step stage: modify insight: "Working backwards from where a corner should end up, and from the image back to the object, shows a translation is a reversible pair of changes." try: { playground: board, starter: "move.yml#free", height: 600 } tasks: - starter: "move.yml#free" hint: ["Compare the x-coordinates of A and A′.", "Then compare the y-coordinates."] check: { type: board, text: "Slide the triangle so that A′ is at (−3, 2).", when: "x(A) = -3 and y(A) = 2", explain: "From (1, 1) to (−3, 2) is 4 left and 1 up." } - starter: "move.yml#free" hint: ["The top corner C needs a y below 0.", "A′ must be to the right of the y-axis."] check: { type: board, text: "Slide the triangle into the fourth quadrant (right of the y-axis, below the x-axis).", when: "x(A) > 0 and y(C) < 0", explain: "For example 2 right and 4 down: every corner has a positive x and a negative y." } - check: type: question q: "A shape is translated 5 right and 3 down. Which translation moves the image back to where it started?" options: ["5 left and 3 up", "5 right and 3 up", "3 left and 5 up", "5 left and 3 down"] answer: 0 feedback: [null, "That undoes only the vertical move.", "x and y changes are swapped.", "That undoes only the horizontal move."] explain: "Undo each part: 5 right becomes 5 left, and 3 down becomes 3 up." - check: type: question q: "A shape is translated 2 right, then 3 up. Another shape is translated 3 up, then 2 right. Do they end up in the same place?" options: ["Yes: the order of the two moves does not matter", "No: the first move is different", "Only if the shapes are triangles"] answer: 0 feedback: [null, "Both add 2 to x and 3 to y.", "It is true for every shape."] explain: "Both change $(x, y)$ to $(x + 2, y + 3)$, so the order does not matter." ``` ### Aim for A′ Work out the change in x, then in y. ### The fourth quadrant ### Undo the move ### Two moves ## Practise: translations ```step stage: practise insight: "Reading images, the move between two points and the quadrant, mixed; left and down not taking away is the planted slip; the quadrant review keeps coordinates fresh." try: { playground: board, starter: "move.yml#free", height: 600 } tasks: - check: type: answer q: "C is at (3, 2). After a translation of 3 right and 2 down, what is the x-coordinate of C′?" answer: "6" feedback: - ["0", "Right adds to x: 3 + 3."] explain: "3 + 3 = 6." - check: type: answer q: "With the same translation, what is the y-coordinate of C′?" answer: "0" feedback: - ["4", "Down takes away from y: 2 − 2."] explain: "2 − 2 = 0, so C′ = (6, 0)." - check: type: question q: "Which translation takes (2, 5) to (−1, 3)?" options: ["3 left and 2 down", "3 right and 2 down", "3 left and 2 up", "1 left and 3 down"] answer: 0 feedback: [null, "Right would make x bigger.", "Up would make y bigger.", "Check the change in x: from 2 to −1."] explain: "x goes from 2 to −1 (3 left); y goes from 5 to 3 (2 down)." smaller: check: type: question q: "Look at x only: it goes from 2 to −1. Did it move left or right?" options: ["Left: x got smaller", "Right: x got bigger"] answer: 0 feedback: [null, "−1 is less than 2, so x got smaller."] explain: "−1 is less than 2, so x moved left. Now do the same with y." - check: type: question q: "Review: in which quadrant is the point (−3, 2)?" options: ["Top left", "Top right", "Bottom left", "Bottom right"] answer: 0 feedback: [null, "A positive x is to the right of the y-axis.", "A positive y is above the x-axis.", "Both signs are wrong for the bottom right."] explain: "A negative x is left of the y-axis and a positive y is above the x-axis." ``` ### The x-coordinate ### The y-coordinate ### Between two points ### Review: quadrants ## Make: a move to the origin ```step stage: make insight: "Finding the translation that puts a chosen corner at the origin makes them reason from the target back to the move." try: { playground: board, starter: "move.yml#free", height: 600 } hint: ["Corner C is at (3, 2).", "Both coordinates must become 0."] check: { type: board, text: "Slide the triangle so that corner C′ lands exactly on the origin (0, 0).", when: "x(C) = 0 and y(C) = 0", explain: "C goes from (3, 2) to (0, 0): 3 left and 2 down." } ``` Then write the translation in words, and as a rule for $(x, y)$. ## Make: a game move, on paper ```step stage: make insight: "A game moves a character by adding to x and y: right adds to x, down takes away from y, and each press repeats the same move." hint: ["Do the right presses first, then the down press.", "Down takes away from y."] check: type: reasoning paper: true q: "In a game, each press of the right arrow moves a character 5 to the right, and each press of the down arrow moves it 3 down (y goes up the screen, as on a maths grid). One corner of the character starts at (2, 6). The player presses right twice, then down once. What is the y-coordinate of the corner now?" steps: - ["Right 5 adds 5 to $x$; down 3 takes 3 from $y$", "each press is one translation"] - ["Right twice: $x = 2 + 5 + 5 = 12$", "$y$ does not change for right"] - ["Down once: $y = 6 - 3 = 3$", "down takes away from $y$"] - ["The corner is now at $(12, 3)$", "$x$ and $y$ are changed separately"] picks: - step: 3 q: "What does 'down 3' do to y?" options: - "Takes 3 away: 6 − 3 = 3" - "Adds 3: 6 + 3 = 9" - "Takes 3 away from x instead" answer: 0 feedback: [null, "Down makes y smaller. Adding 3 would move the corner up.", "Down changes y, not x."] answer: "3" tolerance: 0 feedback: - ["9", "That adds 3 to y. Down takes away."] - ["12", "That is the x-coordinate. The question asks for y."] criteria: - "I changed x for right and y for down, separately." - "I took 3 away from y for down." - "I wrote the new corner as (12, 3)." explain: "Right twice gives x = 2 + 10 = 12. Down once gives y = 6 − 3 = 3. The corner is at (12, 3), so y = 3." ``` Do this one in your book, not on the screen. The moves and the corner are made up for the task; a real game moves the character a little each frame. Write the new x and y after each press, then type the y-coordinate. **Also used in** - **Games.** Moving a character is adding to x and y; a block-coding game does exactly this with its move blocks. - **Lifts and sliding doors.** Every point of a lift or a door moves the same way, which is what makes the move a translation. ```teacher summary: Students slide a triangle on the coordinate plane and describe the move by the change in each coordinate (AC9M7SP03, node 1). time: 35 timing: Predict and Run 8 min · Investigate 8 min · Modify 10 min · Practise and Make 9 min goals: - I can translate a shape and write the new coordinates. - I can describe a translation as so many units left or right and up or down. - I can say what changes and what stays the same. struggle: Left and down mean taking away. Ask students to say, before moving, whether x and y get bigger or smaller. before: > Do the Run board yourself first. Students need to plot and read coordinates in all four quadrants (Year 6). The one idea: every point moves the same way, so the same amount is added to every x and every y. The common mistake is adding for left or down (Ravi's mistake). This is the hinge for the transformations node: a coordinate slip here carries into reflections and rotations, so check the Practise answers. Combining two translations (the last Modify question) is a wider idea. running: - "Predict: ask for the direction of the change in x and in y separately." - "Run: ask what stays the same for all three corners." - "Investigate: ask Ravi's question again with 3 left and 2 down." - "Modify: for the undo question, ask what the opposite of each part is." - "Make: ask for the translation as a rule for (x, y)." - "Paper: the game-move task is worked in books; the page marks y (3) and the reason that down takes away from y. Books out, then look at the page for x and y changed separately." stuck: - see: A student adds when moving left or down. ask: On the x-axis, does a number get bigger or smaller as you go left? fix: Left and down take away; right and up add. - see: A student swaps the x and y changes. ask: Which way does x measure, across or up? fix: x is across, y is up; write the horizontal move first. - see: A student moves only corner A. ask: Where does corner B go? fix: Every corner moves the same way. stretch: Two translations are done one after the other. Write the single translation that does the same, and show that the order does not matter. support: Count squares on the grid for each move before using the sliders. leads: > This starts AC9M7SP03. Where it leads: reflections (next lesson), rotations, then combining transformations and the vector notation for translations in Year 8. exit: q: A (2, 5) is translated 4 left and 3 down. Where is A′? a: "(−2, 2): x is 2 − 4 = −2 and y is 5 − 3 = 2." explain: > A **translation** slides every point of a shape the same distance in the same direction. The **object** becomes the **image**, and A becomes A′. Right and up add; left and down take away. A translation of 3 right and 2 down changes $(x, y)$ to $(x + 3, y - 2)$. ```
